about.title: About me
about.summary: I have my roots in the trades: After completing my apprenticeship in water supply, I took two sabbatical years between 2016 and 2018 to travel the world, teach myself Spanish, and work various jobs. I then joined HMP Heidenhain Microprint in Berlin – a circuit board manufacturer – where I worked with an external team to modernize a legacy control system into a fully automated, PLC-controlled system. This experience sparked my passion for programming, leading me to Robert Bosch GmbH in Nuremberg. There, I completed an apprenticeship as an IT Specialist for Application Development, which I accelerated to 2.5 years and finished with distinction, just like my first trade. I independently established the site's web development infrastructure and became the first full-time developer at the NuP1 manufacturing plant. Today, I develop complex business web applications using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Prisma ORM – some of which are deployed plant-wide, Bosch-wide which is globally.

Migrated legacy C# Blazor projects to modern JavaScript frameworks and created a site-wide web template with Bosch corporate design.

This was my first exposure to programming and sparked my desire to reorient toward becoming a programmer.
